The conditions and the one-sentence definitions of each column are in the "Sparse leaderboard matrix" section of `code/RESULTS.md`. The same text is in my closed issue experiment-repo#6.
  > 
  > The result that carries the claim is that greedy A beats random on the sparse MTEB matrix at every density. The data for it:
  > - `sparse_curves.csv`: std_rmse by k, with a family-clustered CI. Columns are subset, selector (greedyA or random, plus colmean), predictor (fa, pw, softimpute, colmean), k and the CI.
  > - `sparse_closure.csv`: closure by k with CI.
  > - `sparse_gap.csv`: the greedy-A-minus-random gap by k with CI.
  > - `sparse_kstar.csv`: k* at 0.8, 0.9 and 0.95, with a `censored` flag.
  > - `sparse_refs.csv`: the colmean and LOBO references.
  > - `sparse_subsets.csv`: the size and density of each pool.
  > 
  > Suggested figure: closure against k for greedy A and random with `fa` and `pw`, one panel per pool. Use `eng_d30`, `eng_d50`, `eng_d70` and `all_d30` for the main text, and `eng_full` and `all_d50` for an appendix table. Grid points are 1-6, 8, 10, 12, 15, 20. There is no k=30.
  > 
  > Two points to carry into captions and labels. A censored k* means closure 0.9 was not reached on the grid. The LOBO reference is the lower of `fa` and `pw` for all of C predicting T, so closure can exceed 1.
  > 
  > If a figure needs data I have not produced, ask in experiment-repo.
